chunks: With regards to two men differing, so one of them says, 'I was your Imam', and the other one says, 'I was your Imam', so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Both of their Salāt are complete'. So I said, 'Supposing each one of them says, 'I was following you'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Both their Salāt are spoilt, and let them both resume'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the validity of prayer when two people both claim to be the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of *ikhtilaf* (disagreement) in prayer leadership, distinguishing between two claimants where both assert authority—resulting in valid prayers due to the presumption of correctness—versus two humble claimants where both defer to the other, rendering the prayer invalid due to mutual uncertainty. Shia jurists utilize this distinction to derive rules regarding the validity of congregational prayer when the identity of the Imam is ambiguous, emphasizing that the physical presence of a leader suffices for validity unless there is clear evidence of defect. The ruling underscores the Shia legal methodology of preserving the prayer's validity in cases of doubt (*shakk*) while requiring renewal (*isti'naf*) when the structural integrity of the leadership is compromised by mutual subordination.
